paragraphs.text: Expire stale dsh-auth cookies before the 16 KiB header limit (HTTP 431).
# dsh-cookie-janitor
English | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that expires stale
`dsh-auth-*` sign-in cookies before the `Cookie` reques

t header can reach Node's 16 KiB header
limit — the point where the HTTP parser answers `431 Request

Header Fields Too Large` before any
route, handler, or plugin runs.
## The problem it fixes
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection` mints one browser cookie per request **authority**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The name embeds the authority, the lifetime is 30 days (`cookieMaxAgeDays`, default 30), and the
pac

kage never sends a deletion — there is no cleanup path at all. Cookies are **host-scoped, not
port-s

coped**, so every port a browser has used for `dsh web` within those 30 days leaves one more
`dsh-au
th-*` entry in the same jar for `127.0.0.1`.
One pair is about 226 bytes. The parser's limit is 16 KiB of request headers: in testing, a request

whose `Cookie` header was 16,400 bytes returned 431 while 16,200 bytes still reached the
application

. Roughly 69 accumulated cookies are therefore enough to lock the GUI out, and once it
happens nothi
ng in the GUI can recover the page — every request dies before routing.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Directly from this repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart `dsh web` (or the Desktop app) if your host does not hot-apply plugins.
## What it does

On activation the plugin prepends one `request` listener to the listening `http.Server`. For each
re

quest carrying `dsh-auth-*` cookies it measures the `Cookie` header; once the jar crosses the
budget

rrying `dsh-auth-*` cookies it measures the `Cookie` header; once the jar crosses the
budget it adds
[代码示例省略，未执行]

for every cookie that is **not** the current request's own authority, oldest first, keeping
`retain`

of them. The browser drains the jar on that response. The request itself is answered by
the normal

pipeline: the hook only sets headers and never writes one, so routing, authentication,
and the SPA f
allback are untouched.
## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Pruning only starts above the budget, so a jar holding one cookie per live instance is never
touched

. Several live authorities on one host (Desktop plus `dsh web` on port 3080, say) keep
working until

the jar crosses the budget; after that the oldest entries are the ones expired, and a
reaped instan
ce signs in again from its printed URL.
## Manual rescue

`GET /__dsh-cookie-janitor` expires every `dsh-auth-*` cookie the request carries and prints the
obs

erved statistics — largest `Cookie` header, most cookies seen, total pruned. Use it when a jar is
al
ready unusable: open it in the same browser that holds the cookies, then reopen the DSH URL.
## When you do not need it

The Desktop app does not accumulate these cookies: its main window talks to the Host through the
`ds

h-app://app/` protocol handler, which forwards exactly one cookie held in the shell's memory and
wit

hholds `set-cookie` from the page jar (checked against DSH 0.2.1-rc.5). The exposure is the
`web` pr

ofile in a real browser, where the jar is shared across every port used within the cookie
lifetime.

The plugin is harmless where it has nothing to prune — it emits no headers below the
budget.

It also cannot help with a `Cookie` header that is large for reasons other than `dsh-auth-*`
cookies
; those are left alone deliberately.
## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.1-rc.1` or newer on the same 0.2.x line (`engines.dsh`).
- No runtime dependencies, no bu
ild step, no install scripts.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The suite drives the real `apply()` against a fake context and a fake response: budget gating,
`reta

in`, byte-only pruning, `dryRun`, duplicate-pass protection, the rescue route, authority
matching, a
nd config normalization.
